summary: Adds a 'Security Events / Show only Security Event cases' checkbox to the Cases table filter dialog, sent as a security_event_only query param (now accepted by every list endpoint's common parameters); for Case lists the backend then excludes cases that have any linked signal instance (NOT EXISTS SignalInstance.case_id). Despite the label 'cases with a dedicated channel', the backend never looks at the dedicated-channel setting. Also the dialog now pre-fills current filters when opened, and URL filter parsing treats 'true'/'false' as booleans.

statements.why: Read-only list filter, still behind the existing authenticated list endpoints; no permission, data-change or secret issue.

statements.text: The agent changed src/dispatch/static/dispatch/src/case/TableFilterDialog.vue: it now shows "Security Events" and "Show only cases with a dedicated channel".
statements.why: The labels are quoted correctly, but the filter actually shows cases with no signal instances (database/service.py:722-724), not cases with a dedicated channel; an owner would believe it filters by dedicated channel.

statements.text: The agent also changed src/dispatch/database/service.py, .../case/store.js, .../router/utils.js and .../search/utils.js, in ways plain can't describe yet.
statements.why: True but vacuous; the server-side filter in database/service.py is the core of the feature.

misses.what: The new filter doesn't do what its label says: it hides every case linked to a signal (alert) rather than showing cases with a dedicated channel, so users may get unexpected results.
The case filter dialog now opens pre-filled with the currently applied filters (previously opened blank).
